newsitem.title: POLAND: Relieved Poland praises Moscow over Belarus deal.
newsitem.headline: Relieved Poland praises Moscow over Belarus deal.

text.p: Poland's foreign minister expressed relief on Friday over a compromise easing tension in neighbouring Belarus and warmly praised Moscow's role in bringing it about.

"A certain compromise has been reached, which has been greeted with relief by all those who were anxiously observing the situation develop in that country," PAP news agency quoted the minister, Dariusz Rosati, as saying.

A Russian mission headed by Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin earlier succeeded in persuading Belarus President Alexander Lukashenko to agree that a planned Sunday referendum on expanding his powers should not be legally binding.
Lukashenko's opponents in parliament, who have accused him of dictatorial ambitions, in turn agreed to drop impeachment proceedings against him.

"This again confirms what was clear to us from the beginning, that the one country which can effectively bring influence for stabilisation in Belarus is Russia," Rosati said. "Russia assumed this responsibility and played a very important and constructive role."
Poland, which shares a long land border with the former Soviet republic of Belarus and is deeply concerned over developments there, had also tried to influence the situation.
Its President Aleksander Kwasniewski, Lithuania's Algirdas Brazauskas and Ukraine's Leonid Kuchma issued a joint statement on Wednesday calling for a constitutional resolution of the conflict.
